why: Building a BST by hand: insert and search both walk one root-to-leaf path chosen by comparisons, and delete adds the classic three cases (leaf, one child, two children replaced by the inorder successor).
hints: Each operation should touch only one path from the root. How do you decide left or right at each node?

Search: compare and move until you find the key or fall off. Insert: the same walk, then hang a new node where you fell off. Delete: no child or one child splices out; two children copy in the smallest key of the right subtree and delete that node.
Implement the three operations with loops on a small Node class; each costs O(height). Sorted inserts make a chain, which is fine at 5000 operations.
pitfalls: Inserting an existing key must not create a duplicate node.
Deleting the root or a key that is absent are the cases that usually break.
When deleting a two-child node, the successor can have a right child; reattach it to the successor's parent.
